claim: Efficient in vitro transcription by RNA Polymerase II is initiated with six basal transcription factors (TATA binding protein (TBP), TFIIA, TFIIB, TFIIE, TFIIF, TFIIH), Pol II enzyme and TATA-containing promoter DNA.
source: Efficient in vitro transcription by RNA Polymerase II (Pol II) is initiated with six basal transcription factors (TATA binding protein (TBP), TFIIA, TFIIB, TFIIE, TFIIF, TFIIH), Pol II enzyme and TATA-containing promoter DNA.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the requirements for in vitro transcription by RNA Polymerase II.

claim: Cellular mRNA transcription requires one or more coactivator complexes such as Mediator, TFIID, SAGA, NuA4 and Swi/Snf.
source: Cellular mRNA transcription, much of which initiates at non-TATA-containing promoters, also requires one or more coactivator complexes such as Mediator, TFIID, SAGA, NuA4 and Swi/Snf, that either directly contact the basal transcription machinery and/or modify chromatin (Allen and Taatjes, 2015; Doyon and Côté, 2004; Hahn and Young, 2011; Hantsche and Cramer, 2017; Nogales et al., 2017; Rando and Winston, 2012; Sainsbury et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The yeast coactivators SAGA and TFIID share five subunits.
source: The yeast coactivators SAGA and TFIID share five subunits (Grant et al., 1998) but are otherwise unrelated.
evidence: Supported by citation to Grant et al., 1998.

claim: SAGA contains four known activities: activator binding, histone H3-acetylation, histone H2B deubiquitylation and TBP binding.
source: SAGA contains four known activities: activator binding, histone H3-acetylation, histone H2B deubiquitylation and TBP binding (Han et al., 2014; Helmlinger et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2019; Setiaputra et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: SAGA functions as a TBP-DNA loading factor, mediated in part via TFIIA and its TBP-binding subunit Spt3.
source: In addition to performing chromatin modifications, SAGA was recently shown to function as a TBP-DNA loading factor, mediated in part via TFIIA and its TBP-binding subunit Spt3 (Papai et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Papai et al., 2019.

claim: TFIID is a large dynamic complex comprised of TBP and 13–14 Taf (TBP associated factor) subunits.
source: TFIID is a large dynamic complex, comprised of TBP and 13–14 Taf (TBP associated factor) subunits, that functions in activator binding, promoter recognition and PIC formation (Bieniossek et al., 2013; Hahn and Young, 2011; Nogales et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: TFIID can bind one or more short downstream metazoan promoter elements and undergoes large conformational changes while positioning TBP on DNA.
source: Prior studies showed that TFIID can bind one or more short downstream metazoan promoter elements and that it undergoes large conformational changes while positioning TBP on DNA (Kolesnikova et al., 2018; Louder et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kolesnikova et al., 2018 and Louder et al., 2016.

claim: The TFIIA-TFIID-DNA complex seems incompatible with PIC formation based on cryoEM structures.
source: CryoEM structures of human TFIID and TFIIA-TFIID-DNA revealed that this complex seems incompatible with PIC formation (Patel et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Patel et al., 2018.

claim: Several Tafs in the TFIID-DNA complex are in position to clash with TFIIF and Pol II in the PIC.
source: Several Tafs in the TFIID-DNA complex are in position to clash with TFIIF and Pol II in the PIC and the DNA bend in the TFIIA-TFIID-DNA complex is different from that in the closed state PIC.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM structures mentioned in the context.

claim: TFIID, in conjunction with TFIIA, functions as a TBP-loading factor and the Tafs must either dissociate or undergo major rearrangement before PIC assembly.
source: From this it was proposed that TFIID, in conjunction with TFIIA, functions as a TBP-loading factor and that the Tafs must either dissociate or undergo major rearrangement before PIC assembly (Joo et al., 2017; Patel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a proposal based on structural data, supported by citations.

claim: At least some yeast genes can be activated and transcribed after depletion or inactivation of TFIID (Taf) subunits.
source: Early work showed that at least some yeast genes can be activated and transcribed after depletion or inactivation of TFIID (Taf) subunits (Kuras, 2000; Li et al., 2000; Moqtaderi et al., 1996; Walker et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Both TFIID and SAGA contribute to steady state mRNA expression of most yeast genes, but transcription of nearly all genes is dominated by the dependence on either TFIID or SAGA.
source: Pioneering genome-wide studies later suggested that both TFIID and SAGA contribute to steady state mRNA expression of most yeast genes, but that transcription of nearly all genes is dominated by the dependence on either TFIID or SAGA (Huisinga and Pugh, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Huisinga and Pugh, 2004.

claim: The 'TFIID-dominated' class represents approximately 90% of Pol II-transcribed genes, many of which lack a consensus TATA element.
source: From this study, the 'TFIID-dominated' class represented ~ 90% of Pol II-transcribed genes, many of which lacked a consensus TATA element, while the 'SAGA-dominated' genes are enriched for TATA-containing and stress-inducible genes.
evidence: This refers to findings from the Huisinga and Pugh, 2004 study.

claim: The 'SAGA-dominated' genes are enriched for TATA-containing and stress-inducible genes.
source: From this study, the 'TFIID-dominated' class represented ~ 90% of Pol II-transcribed genes, many of which lacked a consensus TATA element, while the 'SAGA-dominated' genes are enriched for TATA-containing and stress-inducible genes.
evidence: This refers to findings from the Huisinga and Pugh, 2004 study.

claim: Promoters from the TFIID-dominated class generally have high levels of TFIID-subunit crosslinking while lower levels of crosslinking are often observed at the SAGA-dominated genes.
source: Formaldehyde crosslinking methods showed that promoters from the TFIID-dominated class generally have high levels of TFIID-subunit crosslinking while lower levels of crosslinking are often observed at the SAGA-dominated genes (Kuras, 2000; Li et al., 2000; Rhee and Pugh, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Mutations affecting genome-wide transcription alter mRNA stability, making prior steady state mRNA measurements used in earlier studies of TFIID and SAGA specificity problematic.
source: First, mutations affecting genome-wide transcription are now known to alter mRNA stability, making prior steady state mRNA measurements used in earlier studies of TFIID and SAGA specificity problematic (Haimovich et al., 2013; Munchel et al., 2011; Sun et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Haimovich et al., 2013; Munchel et al., 2011; Sun et al., 2012.

claim: SAGA modifies chromatin at nearly all expressed genes, rather than only at the SAGA-dominated subset.
source: Second, mapping SAGA-dependent chromatin modifications showed that SAGA modifies chromatin at nearly all expressed genes, rather than only at the SAGA-dominated subset (Bonnet et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bonnet et al., 2014.

claim: Formaldehyde-independent mapping of SAGA and TFIID using the MNase-based ChEC-seq approach identified TFIID and SAGA binding at both gene classes.
source: Third, formaldehyde-independent mapping of SAGA and TFIID using the MNase-based ChEC-seq approach identified TFIID and SAGA binding at both gene classes (Baptista et al., 2017; Grünberg et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Baptista et al., 2017 and Grünberg et al., 2016.

claim: The majority of genes showed decreased transcription upon deletion or depletion of SAGA or TFIID subunits.
source: Finally, native Pol II ChIP and/or analysis of newly synthesized mRNA found that the majority of genes showed decreased transcription upon deletion or depletion of SAGA or TFIID subunits (Baptista et al., 2017; Warfield et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Baptista et al., 2017 and Warfield et al., 2017.

claim: Many genes in the SAGA-dominated class were only modestly sensitive to Taf1 depletion based on analysis of the top 10% of transcribed genes.
source: However, the proposal that TFIID is generally required for transcription was recently disputed based on anchor-away depletion of the TFIID subunit Taf1 (Petrenko et al., 2019). Analysis of the top 10% of transcribed genes, analyzed by Pol II-ChIP, showed that many genes in the SAGA-dominated class were only modestly sensitive to Taf1 depletion.
evidence: Supported by citation to Petrenko et al., 2019.

claim: Deletions within genes coding for subunits of the transcription coactivator SAGA caused strong genome-wide defects in transcription and SAGA-mediated chromatin modifications.
source: Deletions within genes coding for subunits of the transcription coactivator SAGA caused strong genome-wide defects in transcription and SAGA-mediated chromatin modifications.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Rapid SAGA depletion produced only modest transcription defects at 13% of protein-coding genes.
source: In contrast, rapid SAGA depletion produced only modest transcription defects at 13% of protein-coding genes – genes that are generally more sensitive to rapid TFIID depletion.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The 13% of genes affected by rapid SAGA depletion are generally more sensitive to rapid TFIID depletion.
source: In contrast, rapid SAGA depletion produced only modest transcription defects at 13% of protein-coding genes – genes that are generally more sensitive to rapid TFIID depletion.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Transcription of 'coactivator-redundant' genes is strongly affected by rapid depletion of both TFIID and SAGA.
source: However, transcription of these 'coactivator-redundant' genes is strongly affected by rapid depletion of both factors, showing the overlapping functions of TFIID and SAGA at this gene set.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The overlapping function of TFIID and SAGA at coactivator-redundant genes is linked to TBP-DNA recruitment.
source: We suggest that this overlapping function is linked to TBP-DNA recruitment.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings and prior knowledge.

claim: 87% of expressed genes termed 'TFIID-dependent' are highly sensitive to rapid TFIID depletion and insensitive to rapid SAGA depletion.
source: The remaining 87% of expressed genes that we term 'TFIID-dependent' are highly sensitive to rapid TFIID depletion and insensitive to rapid SAGA depletion.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Genome-wide mapping found binding of both SAGA and TFIID at many genes independent of gene class.
source: Genome-wide mapping of SAGA and TFIID found binding of both factors at many genes independent of gene class.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by ChEC-seq data shown in figures.

claim: The distinction between the gene classes is due to multiple components rather than any single regulatory factor or promoter sequence motif.
source: Promoter analysis suggests that the distinction between the gene classes is due to multiple components rather than any single regulatory factor or promoter sequence motif.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on promoter analysis data presented in the study.

claim: The spt3Δ strain showed strong genome-wide transcription defects for nearly all genes.
source: For example, the spt3Δ strain showed strong genome-wide transcription defects for nearly all genes while degron-induced inactivation of Spt3/Spt20 for 30 min caused only modest defects at a small subset of genes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Degron-induced inactivation of Spt3/Spt20 for 30 min caused only modest defects at a small subset of genes.
source: For example, the spt3Δ strain showed strong genome-wide transcription defects for nearly all genes while degron-induced inactivation of Spt3/Spt20 for 30 min caused only modest defects at a small subset of genes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Rapid depletion of Taf13 caused strong genome-wide transcription defects at most genes.
source: Rapid depletion of Taf13, a key TBP-interacting subunit located in TFIID lobe A, caused strong genome-wide transcription defects at most genes as previously observed using native Pol II ChIP (Warfield et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and citation to Warfield et al., 2017.

claim: The changes in gene expression showed poor correlation with a stress-response transcription signature, indicating that the changes observed are not due to a general stress response.
source: For all strains assayed, the changes in gene expression showed poor correlation with a stress-response transcription signature (O'Duibhir et al., 2014), indicating that the changes we observed are not due to a general stress response (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The degron-containing strains showed ≥85% viability after 30 min of IAA treatment.
source: The degron-containing strains showed ≥85% viability after 30 min of IAA treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B) (Warfield et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by viability data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: The TFIID-dependent gene set contains 87% of analyzed genes (4245 genes).
source: The largest cluster, we term 'TFIID-dependent genes' (see reasoning below), contains 87% of analyzed genes (4245 genes) and is most sensitive to TFIID depletion.
evidence: This is based on k-means clustering analysis of the experimental data.

claim: TFIID-dependent genes show a ~4.5 fold average decrease in transcription upon depletion of either Taf13, Taf7 or Taf1.
source: These genes show a ~ 4.5 fold average decrease in transcription upon depletion of ether Taf13, Taf7 or Taf1 (Figure 2A, orange boxes, lanes 8–11).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: TFIID-dependent genes showed genome-wide transcription decreased by an average of ~2.7 fold in the spt3Δ strain.
source: This large gene set was also sensitive to gene deletions in SAGA subunits with genome-wide transcription decreased by an average of ~2.7 fold in the spt3Δ strain with lesser but significant defects observed in the spt7Δ and spt20Δ strains (Figure 2A, orange boxes, lanes 5–7).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Expression of nearly all genes in the 'TFIID-dependent' set showed little or no change upon rapid SAGA subunit depletion using the Spt3/20 and Spt3/7 degron strains.
source: In contrast, expression of nearly all genes in the 'TFIID-dependent' set showed little or no change upon rapid SAGA subunit depletion using the Spt3/20 and Spt3/7 degron strains (Figure 2A, orange boxes, lanes 2–4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The coactivator-redundant gene set contains 13% of analyzed genes (655 genes).
source: The smaller gene set, that we term 'TFIID/SAGA-redundant' (or 'coactivator-redundant' (CR); see reasoning below), contains 13% of analyzed genes (655 genes) and these genes are more sensitive to deletions in SAGA subunits (~3–4 fold decrease) and less sensitive to TFIID depletion (~1.5–2-fold decrease) compared with the TFIID-dependent genes.
evidence: This is based on k-means clustering analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Coactivator-redundant genes are more sensitive to deletions in SAGA subunits (~3–4 fold decrease) and less sensitive to TFIID depletion (~1.5–2-fold decrease) compared with the TFIID-dependent genes.
source: The smaller gene set, that we term 'TFIID/SAGA-redundant' (or 'coactivator-redundant' (CR); see reasoning below), contains 13% of analyzed genes (655 genes) and these genes are more sensitive to deletions in SAGA subunits (~3–4 fold decrease) and less sensitive to TFIID depletion (~1.5–2-fold decrease) compared with the TFIID-dependent genes. (Figure 2A, blue boxes, lanes 5–11).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Coactivator-redundant genes showed only modest transcription defects upon rapid SAGA depletion.
source: Surprisingly, these coactivator-redundant genes showed only modest transcription defects upon rapid SAGA depletion (Figure 2A, blue boxes, lanes 2–7).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The strongest average defect in coactivator-redundant genes was caused by the Spt3/20 degron, with an average transcription decrease of ~1.6 fold.
source: The strongest average defect was caused by the Spt3/20 degron, with an average transcription decrease of ~1.6 fold.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The coactivator-redundant genes are, on average, more sensitive to rapid depletion of TFIID than to rapid SAGA depletion.
source: Surprisingly, comparison of transcription defects caused by rapid TFIID depletion vs rapid SAGA depletion showed that the coactivator-redundant genes are, on average, more sensitive to rapid depletion of TFIID (Figure 2A, blue boxes, lanes 2–4; 8–11).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A ~2 fold average decrease in transcription was observed in the Taf13-degron vs ~1.6 fold decrease in the Spt3/20 degron for coactivator-redundant genes.
source: For example, we observed a ~ 2 fold average decrease in transcription in the Taf13-degron vs ~ 1.6 fold decrease in the Spt3/20 degron.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Simultaneous TFIID and SAGA depletion causes a severe defect in the coactivator-redundant gene set with an average decrease of ~5.7 fold.
source: We found that simultaneous TFIID and SAGA depletion causes a severe defect in the coactivator-redundant gene set with an average decrease of ~5.7 fold (Figure 2B, blue boxes, lanes 4–5; Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A left panel, and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: For nearly all coactivator-redundant genes, the transcription defect upon simultaneous TFIID and SAGA depletion is greater than simply the sum of the defects observed in the Taf13-degron and Spt3/20-degron.
source: For nearly all these genes, the transcription defect is greater than simply the sum of the defects observed in the Taf13-degron and Spt3/20-degron (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), showing that there is substantial redundancy in the ability of TFIID and SAGA to promote transcription of these genes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The TFIID-dependent genes show, on average, no additional defects in the double degron strains compared with the Taf13-degron.
source: In contrast, the TFIID-dependent genes show, on average, no additional defects in the double degron strains compared with the Taf13-degron (Figure 2B, orange boxes, lanes 3–5); Figure 2—figure supplement 1A right panel, and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: After 30 min of IAA treatment, the levels of each degron-tagged Spt subunit in the double degron strain are reduced ~90%.
source: After 30 min of IAA treatment, the levels of each degron-tagged Spt subunit in the double degron strain are reduced ~ 90%, but it is possible that low levels of intact SAGA contribute to genome-wide transcription.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Results from the Spt3/Taf13 and Spt7/Taf13 double degron strains strongly suggest that depletion of only one SAGA subunit is sufficient to inactivate SAGA function.
source: However, results from the Spt3/Taf13 and Spt7/Taf13 double degron strains strongly suggests that depletion of only one SAGA subunit is sufficient to inactivate SAGA function (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The coactivator-redundant genes (655 genes) contain 2/3 of the SAGA-dominated gene set (273 genes) plus an additional 311 genes that were originally characterized as TFIID-dominated.
source: Our coactivator-redundant genes (655 genes) contain 2/3 of the SAGA-dominated gene set (273 genes) plus an additional 311 genes that were originally characterized as TFIID-dominated (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on comparison with previously defined gene categories from Huisinga and Pugh, 2004.

claim: The coactivator-redundant gene set is over 50% different from the SAGA-dominated gene set.
source: Therefore, our coactivator-redundant gene set is over 50% different from the SAGA-dominated gene set.
evidence: This is based on comparison with previously defined gene categories.

claim: The ratio of coactivator-redundant to TFIID-dependent genes is relatively similar across the range of transcribed genes except for the most highly expressed, where the coactivator-redundant class is enriched.
source: When genes are sorted by transcription levels, determined by the amount of 4-thioU incorporated in 5 min, the ratio of coactivator-redundant to TFIID-dependent genes is relatively similar across the range of transcribed genes except for the most highly expressed, where the coactivator-redundant class is enriched (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The bottom four expression quintiles have a relatively constant ratio of ~10% coactivator-redundant genes, but the fraction increases to ~30% in the top quintile and ~44% in the top 10% of expressed genes.
source: The bottom four expression quintiles have a relatively constant ratio of ~10%, but the fraction of genes in the coactivator-redundant category increases to ~30% in the top quintile and ~44% in the top 10% of expressed genes.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The top 2% of expressed genes accounts for ~22% of total transcription.
source: Yeast Pol II transcription is dominated by a small number of very highly transcribed genes: the top 2% of expressed genes accounts for ~22% of total transcription (Figure 3B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B; Supplementary files 1, 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: 47 of the top 50 expressed genes (94%) are in the coactivator-redundant category.
source: As an example of the coactivator bias in these exceptional genes, 47 of the top 50 expressed genes (94%; expression >195 in Figure 3B), are in the coactivator-redundant category (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B and Supplementary file 3.

claim: Most of the coactivator-redundant genes (68%) are more sensitive to Taf13-depletion compared with rapid SAGA depletion (mean difference −0.49).
source: From this plot, it is apparent that most of the coactivator-redundant genes (68%) are more sensitive to Taf13-depletion compared with rapid SAGA depletion (mean difference −0.49).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Among the top 100 expressed coactivator-redundant genes, they are equally divided between stronger TFIID and stronger SAGA-dependence (mean difference −0.07).
source: This difference changes slightly when considering only the top 100 expressed genes that are equally divided between stronger TFIID and stronger SAGA-dependence (mean difference −0.07).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: 60% of coactivator-redundant genes are classified as TATA-containing.
source: Our analysis shows that 60% of coactivator-redundant genes are classified as TATA-containing but that both the coactivator-redundant and TFIID-dependent gene sets contain a nearly equal number of TATA-containing genes using the above criteria.
evidence: This is based on analysis of TATA motifs in promoters, shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Both the coactivator-redundant and TFIID-dependent gene sets contain a nearly equal number of TATA-containing genes.
source: Our analysis shows that 60% of coactivator-redundant genes are classified as TATA-containing but that both the coactivator-redundant and TFIID-dependent gene sets contain a nearly equal number of TATA-containing genes using the above criteria.
evidence: This is based on analysis of TATA motifs in promoters, shown in Figure 3D.

claim: De novo motif discovery found that the binding motifs for 14 transcription factors are preferentially enriched in one of the two gene classes.
source: This analysis found that the binding motifs for 14 transcription factors are preferentially enriched in one of the two gene classes (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is based on de novo motif discovery analysis.

claim: The binding motif for the general regulatory factor Reb1 is found near 18% of the TFIID-dependent genes vs 6% of all other genes.
source: For example, the binding motif for the general regulatory factor Reb1 is found near 18% of the TFIID-dependent genes vs 6% of all other genes while TATA, Msn2 and other motifs are preferentially enriched near the coactivator-redundant genes vs all other genes.
evidence: This is based on motif discovery analysis.

claim: TATA, Msn2 and other motifs are preferentially enriched near the coactivator-redundant genes vs all other genes.
source: For example, the binding motif for the general regulatory factor Reb1 is found near 18% of the TFIID-dependent genes vs 6% of all other genes while TATA, Msn2 and other motifs are preferentially enriched near the coactivator-redundant genes vs all other genes.
evidence: This is based on motif discovery analysis.

claim: The coactivator-redundant genes are clearly enriched for TATA (65% contain this motif) while the TATA motif is found in only ~1/4 of the TFIID-dependent genes.
source: However, the coactivator-redundant genes are clearly enriched for TATA (65% contain this motif) while the TATA motif is found in only ~ 1/4 of the TFIID-dependent genes.
evidence: This is based on direct search for TATA consensus motifs, shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The Msn2/4 motif is enriched in the coactivator-redundant genes compared with the TFIID-dependent genes, although over three times the number of TFIID-dependent genes contain Msn2/4 motifs compared with coactivator-redundant genes (173 vs 609).
source: We also found that the Msn2/4 motif is enriched in the coactivator-redundant genes compared with the TFIID-dependent genes, although over three times the number of TFIID-dependent genes contain Msn2/4 motifs compared with coactivator-redundant genes (173 vs 609).
evidence: This is based on direct search for Msn2/4 consensus motifs, shown in Figure 3E.

claim: 95% of the ribosomal protein (RP) genes belong to the TFIID-dependent category.
source: Although 95% of the RP genes belong to the TFIID-dependent category they show comparable transcription defects upon TFIID depletion as the rest of the TFIID-dependent genes.
evidence: This is based on analysis of RP genes in the dataset.

claim: RP genes show comparable transcription defects upon TFIID depletion as the rest of the TFIID-dependent genes.
source: Although 95% of the RP genes belong to the TFIID-dependent category they show comparable transcription defects upon TFIID depletion as the rest of the TFIID-dependent genes.
evidence: This is based on analysis of RP genes in the dataset.

claim: 83% of the RP genes are found in expression quintile 5.
source: However, RP genes are clearly more highly expressed than the average gene, with 83% of the RP genes found in expression quintile 5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Elimination of HAT function (gcn5Δ) led to a genome-wide transcription defect in both gene classes that was nearly as strong as that found in the spt3Δ mutant.
source: We found that elimination of HAT function (gcn5Δ) led to a genome-wide transcription defect in both gene classes that was nearly as strong as that found in the spt3Δ mutant.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Elimination of deubiquitination function (ubp8Δ) led to more modest genome-wide defects in transcription for both gene classes.
source: Elimination of deubiquitination function (ubp8Δ) led to more modest genome-wide defects in transcription for both gene classes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The spt3Δ, spt20Δ and spt7Δ strains all had lower total levels of H3K18-Ac, ranging from ~34% of normal in the spt7Δ and spt20Δ strains to 70% of normal in the spt3Δ strain.
source: Western blot analyses of whole cell extracts showed that the spt3Δ, spt20Δ and spt7Δ strains all had lower total levels of H3K18-Ac, ranging from ~ 34% of normal in the spt7Δ and spt20Δ strains to 70% of normal in the spt3Δ strain (Figure 5A, left panel; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: H2B-Ub levels were decreased in the spt3Δ, spt20Δ and spt7Δ strains with values ranging from 16 to 29% of WT.
source: H2B-Ub levels were also decreased in these mutants with values ranging from 16 to 29% of WT (Figure 5A, right panel; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Higher levels of H2B-Ub are observed upon deletion of UBP8, encoding the H2B deubiquitinase.
source: As expected, higher levels of H2B-Ub are observed upon deletion of UBP8, encoding the H2B deubiquitinase.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Upon activation of the Spt3/20 or Spt3/7 degrons, H3K18-Ac was >70% of WT levels after 30 min and thereafter decreased slowly over time.
source: In contrast, upon activation of the Spt3/20 or Spt3/7 degrons, H3K18-Ac was >70% of WT levels after 30 min and thereafter decreased slowly over time (Figure 5B, left panel; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: At 6 hr after IAA addition to the Spt3/20 or Spt3/7 degron strains, the levels of H3K18-Ac mark in bulk chromatin were reduced to 45–50% of WT.
source: At 6 hr after IAA addition to these strains, the levels of H3K18-Ac mark in bulk chromatin were reduced to 45–50% of WT.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The levels of H2B-Ub did not show any consistent changes during the time course after degron activation.
source: The levels of H2B-Ub did not show any consistent changes during this time course (Figure 5B, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: There was a >10 fold average defect in promoter-linked H3 acetylation in the gcn5Δ and spt7Δ strains and a 3.3-fold defect in the spt3Δ strain.
source: We found a > 10 fold average defect in promoter-linked H3 acetylation in the gcn5Δ and spt7Δ strains and a 3.3-fold defect in the spt3Δ strain.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: After 30 min of SAGA depletion, there was only a 1.7-fold reduction in promoter-linked H3 acetylation.
source: In contrast, after 30 min of SAGA depletion, we observed only a 1.7-fold reduction.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Changes in H3 acetylation were nearly the same at both the TFIID-dependent and coactivator-redundant genes.
source: These changes in H3 acetylation were nearly the same at both the TFIID-dependent and coactivator-redundant genes (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B), consistent with earlier findings that SAGA contributes to chromatin modifications at all expressed genes (Bonnet et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and citation to Bonnet et al., 2014.

claim: Little or no H3 acetylation change was observed in the ubp8Δ strain.
source: As expected, little or no H3 acetylation change was observed in the ubp8Δ strain.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Using the updated ChEC-seq method to map Taf1, Taf7 and Taf13 binding, 2938, 3681 and 3723 bound mRNA promoters were identified.
source: Using our updated ChEC-seq method to map Taf1, Taf7 and Taf13 binding (four biological replicates each), we identified 2938, 3681 and 3723 bound mRNA promoters, with extensive overlap between binding sites mapped with different Taf-MNase fusions (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) (Supplementary file 8).
evidence: This is supported by ChEC-seq data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: ~75% of TFIID binding sites identified by ChIP-exo overlap with the sites identified by Taf1-MNase.
source: Using the above computational criteria,~75% of TFIID binding sites identified by ChIP-exo (Vinayachandran et al., 2018) overlap with the sites identified by Taf1-MNase, showing a close correspondence in results between our updated ChEC-seq approach and ChIP-exo (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of ChEC-seq and ChIP-exo data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ChEC-seq using Spt3-MNase and Spt7-MNase identified 1601 and 3536 promoter binding sites for SAGA.
source: We next used ChEC-seq to revisit genome-wide binding of SAGA, where Spt3-MNase and Spt7-MNase identified 1601 and 3536 promoter binding sites (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) (Supplementary file 8).
evidence: This is supported by ChEC-seq data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: ~97% of SAGA binding sites mapped using Spt3-MNase overlap with the more extensive set of promoters mapped using Spt7-MNase.
source: Our analysis showed that ~97% of SAGA binding sites mapped using Spt3-MNase overlap with the more extensive set of promoters mapped using Spt7-MNase (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by ChEC-seq data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There was widespread promoter binding and ≥86% overlap in genes bound by TFIID and SAGA when comparing ChEC signals from Taf7 and Spt7-MNase fusions.
source: Importantly, we found widespread promoter binding and ≥ 86% overlap in genes bound by TFIID and SAGA when comparing ChEC signals from Taf7 and Spt7-MNase fusions, supporting our findings above that most genes are regulated by both factors (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by ChEC-seq data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: There was little or no preference for the binding of TFIID or SAGA to either promoter class.
source: Further analysis showed little or no preference for the binding of TFIID or SAGA to either promoter class (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by ChEC-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: In the SPT deletion strains, uninduced transcription at three Gcn4 target genes was decreased >4 fold compared with WT.
source: At the three Gcn4 target genes, uninduced transcription was decreased > 4 fold compared with WT and the response to SM was dependent on the SPT deletion.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: In the WT strain, activation of ARG3, HIS4, and ARG5 ranges from 2.6 to 3.8-fold upon SM addition.
source: In the WT strain, activation of ARG3, HIS4, and ARG5 ranges from 2.6 to 3.8-fold (Figure 7A, compare light and dark blue bars).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: In the spt7Δ strain, the three Gcn4-dependent genes showed some activation (1.7 to 2.5-fold), while activation was eliminated in the spt3Δ strain.
source: Although the levels of both uninduced and activated transcription were reduced in the spt7Δ strain, the three Gcn4-dependent genes showed some activation (1.7 to 2.5-fold; light vs dark gray bars), while activation was eliminated in the spt3Δ strain (light vs dark orange bars).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Cells containing the Spt3/7 double degrons treated with IAA for 30 min before SM induction still allowed for greater than normal fold-activation upon subsequent SM addition (3.6 to 6.9-fold).
source: To determine the consequence of rapid SAGA depletion before transcription was induced, cells containing the Spt3/7 double degrons were first treated with IAA for 30 min to deplete these proteins and then induced with SM for 60 min. This treatment still allowed for greater than normal fold-activation upon subsequent SM addition (3.6 to 6.9-fold; Figure 7B; light vs dark orange bars; Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: IAA added to already SM-induced cells reduced Gcn4-dependent transcription between 1.7 and 2.6-fold.
source: In contrast, IAA added to already SM-induced cells reduced Gcn4-dependent transcription between 1.7 and 2.6-fold (light vs dark gray bars).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: For Gcn4-dependent gene activation, the gene-specific role of SAGA is most important for efficiency or maintenance of ongoing transcription rather than for induction of transcription in response to an activation signal.
source: Combined, our results show that, for Gcn4-dependent gene activation, the gene-specific role of SAGA is most important for efficiency or maintenance of ongoing transcription rather than for induction of transcription in response to an activation signal.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7.

claim: TFIID and SAGA function is substantially redundant at coactivator-redundant genes, with WT expression levels promoted by both coactivators.
source: Our new results bring together many of these findings and provide a new mechanistic explanation for many genes that showed significant Taf-independent expression in earlier studies: TFIID and SAGA function is substantially redundant at these genes, with WT expression levels promoted by both coactivators.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the experimental data.

claim: SAGA has two separable functions in gene expression: (1) a general function important for transcription of nearly all genes revealed by deletions in genes encoding key SAGA subunits, and (2) a gene-specific role revealed by rapid depletion of SAGA function, where only 13% of genes are modestly affected.
source: We find that SAGA has two separable functions in gene expression: (1) a general function important for transcription of nearly all genes. This function was revealed by deletions in genes encoding key SAGA subunits. (2) a gene-specific role revealed by rapid depletion of SAGA function, where only 13% of genes are modestly affected.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the experimental data.

claim: The role of SAGA in global transcription is strongly linked to SAGA-dependent chromatin modifications, particularly Gcn5-dependent H3 acetylation.
source: We further found that the role of SAGA in global transcription is strongly linked to SAGA-dependent chromatin modifications, particularly Gcn5-dependent H3 acetylation.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the experimental data.

claim: Gcn5-dependent H3 acetylation is required for efficient global transcription.
source: This mark, that we find is required for efficient global transcription, is significantly reduced in the SPT deletions but declines only slowly in the rapid depletion experiments.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing transcription defects in gcn5Δ and changes in H3 acetylation.

claim: The TFIID-dependent genes exclusively require Tafs for promoter recognition and TBP-DNA loading while the coactivator-redundant genes can use either SAGA or TFIID.
source: Based on earlier studies, we propose that the TFIID-dependent genes exclusively require Tafs for promoter recognition and TBP-DNA loading while the coactivator-redundant genes can use either SAGA or TFIID.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings and prior knowledge.

claim: SAGA can recruit TBP more directly at many CR genes, taking advantage of specific TBP-TATA interactions and direct TBP interactions with other TBP-compatible DNA binding motifs.
source: Since many CR genes contain TATA elements, we envision that SAGA can recruit TBP more directly, taking advantage of: (1) specific TBP-TATA interactions and (2) direct TBP interactions with other TBP-compatible DNA binding motifs.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings.

claim: Some TBP mutants defective in TATA-DNA binding may be defective in the SAGA-mediated TBP loading pathway but still function in the TFIID-dependent pathway.
source: This model can explain the surprising viability of strains with TBP mutations that are defective in TATA-DNA binding (Kamenova et al., 2014). Some of these TBP mutants may be defective in the SAGA-mediated TBP loading pathway but still function in the TFIID-dependent pathway.
evidence: This is a proposed explanation based on the model and citation to Kamenova et al., 2014.

claim: Rapid depletion of SAGA primarily decreases ongoing and already activated transcription at several coactivator-redundant genes.
source: Finally, we found that rapid depletion of SAGA, primarily decreases ongoing and already activated transcription at several coactivator-redundant genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Rapid depletion of SAGA does not affect activation per se at three Gcn4-dependent genes.
source: In contrast, rapid depletion does not affect activation per se at three Gcn4-dependent genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The TFIID-directed pathway does not seem inherently limiting for relatively high transcription levels.
source: With the exception of the top 50 expressed genes, there are many genes in the top expression quintile that are TFIID-dependent and SAGA-independent. Therefore, the TFIID-directed pathway does not seem inherently limiting for relatively high transcription levels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression data.

claim: Efficient TBP-DNA loading may be important for transcription reinitiation at the coactivator-redundant genes.
source: Efficient TBP-DNA loading may be important for this process at the coactivator-redundant genes and it will be of interest in future studies to probe these genes for defects in initiation, reinitiation and other steps in the transcription pathway after SAGA depletion.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions.
